title: The Great Siege: Malta 1565
author: Ernle Bradford
description: Ernle Bradford’s classic, fast-moving account of the 1565 siege, told from both sides of the walls. Bradford, a sailor and historian, lived on Malta for years.

title: Empires of the Sea
author: Roger Crowley
description: Roger Crowley’s history of the struggle between the Ottoman Empire and Christian Europe for the Mediterranean in the 1500s, from Rhodes to the siege of Malta and the naval battle of Lepanto.

title: Caravaggio: A Life Sacred and Profane
author: Andrew Graham-Dixon
description: Art critic Andrew Graham-Dixon’s biography of Caravaggio, including his year in Malta: his welcome by the knights, his paintings for their church, and his escape from their prison.

title: Fortress Malta: An Island Under Siege, 1940–1943
author: James Holland
description: Historian James Holland’s account of the wartime siege, built from the memories of pilots, sailors, soldiers, and Maltese civilians who lived through the bombing in the shelters under the city.

title: V.
author: Thomas Pynchon
description: Thomas Pynchon’s first novel follows a search for a mysterious woman known as V. across the century. Its climax is set in Valletta, during the 1919 riots and again during the Second World War.

title: A Death in Malta
author: Paul Caruana Galizia
description: Daphne Caruana Galizia’s son Paul, also a journalist, on his mother’s life and work, her murder in 2017, and the family’s long fight to find out who ordered it.
